title: Parkio Daily for August 11, 2026
teaser: Magic Kingdom bus pickups moved at Fort Wilderness; Hollywood Studios closes early Oct. 15; new Tomorrowland tee at Disneyland Resort.

bignews.title: Magic Kingdom bus service rerouted at Fort Wilderness
bignews.body: Buses to Magic Kingdom and Wilderness Lodge are temporarily picking up at a different stop instead of the usual Settlement Bus Depot. The resort has not announced how long the change will last.

parkioInsight.text: Guests staying at Fort Wilderness should allow an extra 10–15 minutes for morning rope drop. The alternate pickup location tends to add walking time from most campsites.

bignews.title: Hollywood Studios closing four hours early for private event in October
bignews.body: The park will close early on a Tuesday in October for a private event. Specific date and details have not been released.

parkioInsight.text: Check your park calendar before booking October trips. Early closures usually mean reduced attraction capacity and heavier waits in the morning hours.

bignews.title: Trick-or-treating strategy shifts at Mickey's Not-So-Scary Halloween Party
bignews.body: The optimal window for candy collection at the Halloween party has changed this year. Previous recommendations no longer apply.

parkioInsight.text: Party attendees may find shorter lines at treat stations during the first parade of the evening. Mid-event windows tend to clear out as guests line up for entertainment.

bignews.title: Disney gift cards no longer accepted at select Walt Disney World locations
bignews.body: Multiple Walt Disney World locations have stopped accepting Disney gift cards. The company has not clarified which spots are affected or whether the change is permanent.

parkioInsight.text: Guests budgeting with gift cards should confirm acceptance before ordering. Carrying a backup payment method is likely the safest move for now.

topstories.title: Disneyland 70th anniversary theming wraps up with six closures ahead
topstories.body: Disneyland has begun removing full-year anniversary decorations after 15 months. Six attraction closures are scheduled to follow the celebration's end.

parkioInsight.text: Guests hoping to see anniversary elements should visit soon. Park-wide refurbishments often mean reduced ride capacity and longer waits for open attractions.

topstories.title: Solar-powered trash cans expanding across Walt Disney World
topstories.body: Smart solar trash and recycling cans are rolling out to more areas of Walt Disney World after an initial test phase. The new units replace older park bins.

parkioInsight.text: The new bins are typically easier to spot in crowded areas. Guests looking for recycling options will likely find clearer labeling than on older units.

topstories.title: EPCOT store refreshed for Halloween season
topstories.body: An underrated EPCOT retail location has added Halloween merchandise and decor. The update is part of the park's seasonal rollout.

parkioInsight.text: Seasonal items at smaller EPCOT shops tend to sell out slower than at flagship stores. Midday shopping often avoids the morning rush.

topstories.title: Muppets souvenir cup sold out at Hollywood Studios after one week
topstories.body: A popular Muppets-themed drink cup has disappeared from Hollywood Studios shelves just days after its debut. The item sold out faster than expected.

parkioInsight.text: Limited-run collectibles at Hollywood Studios often vanish within days. Guests chasing new releases should plan a merchandise stop within the first hour of park opening.

topstories.title: Disney Lakeshore Lodge construction adds bridge and exterior finishes
topstories.body: A new pedestrian bridge and nature murals are taking shape at Disney Lakeshore Lodge along Bay Lake. The Disney Vacation Club resort remains under construction.

parkioInsight.text: Guests staying near Fort Wilderness or the Contemporary can likely catch views of the new resort from Bay Lake watercraft. Evening boat trips tend to offer the clearest sightlines.

topstories.title: Wait times down despite higher attendance at Walt Disney World
topstories.body: Recent shoulder season and summer data show shorter attraction waits even as the company reports modest attendance gains. Both trends appear to be accurate.

parkioInsight.text: More guests are spreading out across parks and arriving at off-peak hours. Mid-afternoon and dinner windows often see lighter queues than traditional rope drop rushes.

topstories.title: D23 Parks Panel details released with tempered expectations
topstories.body: Disney announced the lineup and format for the marquee Parks Panel at D23 Expo, subtly resetting fan hopes for major announcements. The event covers all Disney parks worldwide.

parkioInsight.text: Guests planning 2027 trips may want to hold off on finalizing dates until after D23. New attraction or land announcements tend to shift crowd patterns months in advance.

icymi.title: Tomorrowland Space Mountain shirt arrives at Disneyland Resort
icymi.body: A sparkly pale blue tee featuring Space Mountain and Tomorrowland branding is now on shelves. The shirt retails for $39.99.

icymi.title: Sorcerer Mickey wand holder on sale at Disneyland
icymi.body: A sculpted display stand for custom crystal wands is available at Cristal d'Orleans in New Orleans Square. The holder is priced at $99.

icymi.title: Character Spirit Jersey featuring Pixar favorites debuts at Walt Disney World
icymi.body: A pale blue Spirit Jersey with Remy, Woody, Lightning McQueen, and other animated characters is now in stock at Magic Kingdom. The jersey is $79.99.

icymi.title: Disney Cruise Line extends savings offer through spring 2027
icymi.body: A promotion offering up to $1,500 off select sailings has been expanded to cover late 2026 and spring 2027 voyages. Eligible ships and dates are now available.

spotlight.title: Six Ravens menu fully revealed at Disney Springs
spotlight.body: The new restaurant at Disney Springs has released its complete menu ahead of opening. Dining reviews highlight standout items and unique culinary touches across 50-plus creations.

parkioInsight.text: New Disney Springs restaurants typically see walk-up waits of 60–90 minutes during the first few weeks. Booking a reservation or arriving before 5pm often cuts the line.
